steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: I have a colleague. She speaks four languages.

steps.label: Pronombre sujeto
steps.sentence: I have a colleague **who** speaks four languages.
steps.change: “She” se reemplaza por “who”; no se puede quitar porque es el sujeto.

steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: This is the film. We saw it last night.

steps.label: Pronombre objeto
steps.sentence: This is the film **(that)** we saw last night.
steps.change: “it” desaparece; “that” es objeto, así que puedes omitirlo.

B1-1-0.title: ¿Who, which, that… o nada?
B1-1-0.question: ¿A qué se refiere el pronombre y qué función cumple en su cláusula?

branches.if: Es una persona y es el sujeto
branches.example: The woman who called left a message.

branches.if: Es una cosa y es el sujeto
branches.example: It’s an app that works offline.

branches.if: Es objeto (persona o cosa): después viene otro sujeto
branches.example: The book (that) I lent you is mine.

branches.if: Indica posesión
branches.example: That’s the colleague whose laptop was stolen.

items.b: The song that I like it.
items.note: La segunda está mal: “that” ya es el objeto, no repitas “it”.

items.a: The people who work here are kind.
items.b: The people work here are kind.
items.note: Sin “who” la frase no tiene sentido: el pronombre sujeto no se puede omitir.
“Which” nunca se usa para personas.

B1-1-1.title: De la situación a la reacción

steps.label: Situación
steps.sentence: People cancel at the last minute.

steps.label: It + verbo + objeto
steps.sentence: **It annoys me when** people cancel at the last minute.
steps.change: “It” es un sujeto vacío; la reacción va primero.

steps.label: It + be + adjetivo
steps.sentence: **It’s frustrating when** people cancel at the last minute.

steps.label: Invertida
steps.sentence: **When** people cancel at the last minute, **it** really annoys me.

items.example: It bothers me when people are late.
It annoys me when the wifi drops.
It’s frustrating when nobody answers.
It upsets me when people lie.
It drives me crazy when he chews loudly.

items.a: It bothers me when he arrives late.
items.b: It bothers me when he will arrive late.
items.note: La segunda está mal: después de “when” va presente simple, no “will”.

items.a: It’s annoying when the bus is late.
items.b: It’s annoying me when the bus is late.
items.note: “It’s annoying” es general; “it’s annoying me” solo describe algo que pasa ahora mismo.
Con “when” hablas de algo que se repite; con “that” comentas un hecho concreto.

steps.label: Gerundio como sujeto
steps.change: El verbo en -ing funciona como sustantivo y lleva verbo en singular.

steps.label: Tras preposición
steps.change: Después de una preposición siempre va -ing.

B1-2-0.title: ¿-ing o to + verbo?
B1-2-0.question: ¿Dónde aparece el verbo en la frase?

branches.if: Es el sujeto de la frase
branches.example: Cooking for ten people is exhausting.

branches.if: Va después de una preposición (in, at, of, before…)
branches.example: She’s good at solving problems.

branches.if: Va después de enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest…
branches.example: I avoid driving at night.

branches.if: Va después de want, hope, plan, decide…
branches.example: I decided to change jobs.

items.note: El sujeto con gerundio siempre es singular: “is”, aunque diga “reports”.
Después de preposición va -ing, nunca la forma base.

items.a: Not knowing the answer was hard.
items.b: Knowing not the answer was hard.
items.note: La negación va antes del gerundio.

branches.if: Un adjetivo
branches.example: This route is shorter and more scenic than that one.

branches.if: Un sustantivo contable
branches.example: This city has fewer parks than mine.

branches.if: Un sustantivo incontable
branches.example: There’s less traffic on Sundays.

branches.if: Un verbo
branches.example: She works harder than I do.

B1-2-1.title: Qué tan grande es la diferencia

items.example: It’s slightly cheaper than the other one.
This flat is a bit bigger.
The new model is much faster.
Bogotá is a lot colder than Cartagena.
This hotel is far more expensive.
My car is nowhere near as fast as yours.

items.note: “Fewer” con contables (people); “less” con incontables (noise).
Con verbos, “more” va después del verbo.

items.a: The office is better organised now.
items.b: The office is more organiseder now.
items.note: Con participios usa more / better / worse delante, sin -er.

items.example: Can you open the window?
Could you open the window?
Would you open the window, please?
Could you possibly open the window?
Would you mind opening the window?

items.word: I’d appreciate it if you could…
items.example: I’d appreciate it if you could open the window.

B1-3-0.title: ¿Pides algo para ti o al otro?
B1-3-0.question: ¿Quién va a hacer la acción?

branches.if: Yo (pido permiso)
branches.use: Can / Could / May I…? · Do you mind if I + presente?
branches.example: Do you mind if I sit here?

branches.if: Yo, con más cortesía
branches.use: Would you mind if I + pasado?
branches.example: Would you mind if I opened the window?

branches.if: La otra persona
branches.example: Could you send me the file?

branches.if: La otra persona, muy cortés
branches.example: Would you mind sending me the file?

items.note: Después de “mind” va -ing, nunca “to”.

items.a: Do you mind if I sit here?
items.b: Would you mind if I sat here?
items.note: Las dos son correctas: con “would” el verbo va en pasado y suena más cortés.

items.a: — Would you mind helping? — Not at all.
items.note: “Not at all” significa “con gusto”; “Yes” significaría que sí te molesta.

steps.label: Indirecta
steps.change: Desaparece “does” y la -s pasa al verbo; orden sujeto + verbo.

steps.label: Indirecta (sí/no)
steps.sentence: Could you tell me **if the museum is** open?
steps.change: Las preguntas de sí/no usan “if” o “whether”.

B1-3-1.title: ¿Cómo empiezo la pregunta indirecta?
B1-3-1.question: ¿Qué tipo de pregunta es la original?

branches.if: Tiene palabra wh- con be o modal
branches.example: Could you tell me where the station is?

branches.if: Tiene do / does / did
branches.example: Do you know when the train left?

branches.if: Se responde con sí o no
branches.example: I wonder whether she got my message.

items.a: Do you know where the station is?
items.b: Do you know where is the station?
items.note: No inviertas dos veces: dentro va orden de afirmación.

items.a: Can you tell me what it costs?
items.b: Can you tell me what does it cost?
items.note: “Does” desaparece en la pregunta indirecta.
Si la frase empieza con “I wonder”, termina en punto, no en signo de pregunta.

steps.label: Fondo (en progreso)
steps.change: was / were + -ing: algo que estaba pasando.

steps.label: Evento que interrumpe
steps.change: Pasado simple para la acción corta.

steps.label: Orden invertido
steps.sentence: **When** the phone rang, I was cooking.

B1-4-0.title: ¿Pasado continuo o simple?
B1-4-0.question: ¿Qué papel tiene la acción en tu historia?

branches.if: Estaba en progreso, es el fondo
branches.example: It was raining and everyone was rushing.

branches.if: Es un evento corto y terminado
branches.example: The alarm went off.

branches.if: Es un verbo de estado (know, want, own)
branches.example: I knew the answer.

branches.if: Es un plan que no se cumplió
branches.example: I was going to call you, but I forgot.

items.a: When she arrived, I was cooking.
items.note: En la primera ya estaba cocinando; en la segunda empecé a cocinar después de que llegó.

items.a: I was reading a book yesterday.
items.note: La primera es una actividad en progreso; la segunda dice que lo terminaste.
“Know” es un verbo de estado: no se usa en continuo.

steps.label: Dos eventos en orden
steps.sentence: The ship left. Then we arrived.

steps.label: Empezando por el más reciente
steps.sentence: When we arrived, the ship **had left**.
steps.change: La acción anterior va en had + participio.

steps.label: Con by the time
steps.sentence: **By the time** we arrived, the ship **had already left**.

steps.label: Negativa
steps.sentence: When we arrived, the ship **hadn’t left yet**.
steps.change: “Yet” va al final en la negativa.

items.b: When I arrived, she had left.
items.note: En la primera, se fue al llegar yo; en la segunda, ya se había ido antes.

items.a: After I sent it, she called.
items.b: After I had sent it, she called.
items.note: Las dos son correctas: “after” ya muestra el orden, el pasado perfecto es opcional.

items.a: I was tired because I didn’t sleep.
items.b: I was tired because I hadn’t slept.
items.note: La segunda es más clara: la causa ocurrió antes del cansancio.

branches.if: En el mismo orden en que pasaron
branches.example: I woke up, had breakfast and left.

branches.if: Mencionas primero el más reciente
branches.example: I missed the bus. I had woken up late.

branches.if: Con by the time o antes de un momento pasado
branches.example: By six o’clock, we had finished.

branches.if: Con after / before que ya marcan el orden
branches.example: Before she left, she locked the door.

steps.label: Con cláusula relativa
steps.change: Sustantivo + that + cláusula = un solo bloque.

steps.label: Como sujeto
steps.sentence: **The rule that nobody explains** is the most important one.
steps.change: Todo el bloque es el sujeto de la frase.

steps.label: Concordancia
steps.sentence: **The list** of names that arrived **is** long.
steps.change: El verbo concuerda con “the list”, no con “names”.

items.es: la mayoría de la gente que

items.a: The kind of person who complains…
items.b: The kinds of people who complain…
items.note: Singular o plural según lo que quieres decir.
Con anything, something, everything se prefiere “that” (o nada).

items.a: Most people who live here are friendly.
items.b: Most people who live here is friendly.
items.note: El verbo concuerda con “people” (plural).

items.example: It’s the custom to bring flowers.
It isn’t acceptable to shout.
You’re supposed to sign in.
Staff are expected to wear badges.
You have to show your ID.

branches.if: Una tradición de toda una sociedad
branches.example: It’s the custom to eat tamales at Christmas.

branches.if: Lo que se espera de una persona
branches.use: be supposed to / be expected to
branches.example: Guests are expected to arrive on time.

branches.if: Si un comportamiento está bien visto
branches.example: It’s not acceptable to answer calls at dinner.

branches.if: Algo que debías hacer pero no hiciste
branches.example: I was supposed to call her yesterday.

items.a: You’re supposed to arrive at eight.
items.b: You have to arrive at eight.
items.note: La primera es una expectativa; la segunda, una regla.

items.b: I was supposed to call her.
items.note: En pasado, normalmente significa que no lo hiciste.
La primera describe una tradición; la segunda pone la expectativa sobre ti.

steps.label: Participio después de be
steps.change: Te enfocas en el estado del objeto.

steps.label: Sustantivo con have
steps.sentence: The screen **has a crack** in it.
steps.change: Otra forma de nombrar el daño.

items.note: Con there is / there are, el verbo concuerda con el sustantivo.
“Broken” puede ser “en pedazos” o “que no funciona”; la segunda es más precisa.
“Tear” es irregular: el participio es “torn”.

steps.label: La cosa como sujeto (pasivo)
steps.change: Un poco más formal; significa lo mismo.

steps.label: Problema que se repite
steps.change: keep + -ing = pasa una y otra vez.

B1-6-1.title: ¿Qué estructura necesito?
B1-6-1.question: ¿Quién es el sujeto de tu frase?

branches.if: La persona que hará la acción
branches.example: I need to clean the filter.

branches.if: La cosa que necesita la acción (informal)
branches.example: The filter needs cleaning.

branches.if: La cosa que necesita la acción (formal)
branches.example: The filter needs to be cleaned.

branches.if: Un problema que se repite
branches.example: The engine keeps stalling.

items.note: Elige: “needs replacing” o “needs to be replaced”, nunca una mezcla.
En la forma pasiva falta “to”.
Después de “keep” siempre va -ing.

steps.label: Con causa
steps.sentence: The roof has been repaired **because of** the storm.

B1-7-0.title: ¿Because o because of?
B1-7-0.question: ¿Qué viene después de la palabra de causa?

branches.if: Una cláusula (sujeto + verbo)
branches.example: It was delayed because it rained.

branches.if: Un sustantivo o gerundio
branches.example: It was delayed due to the rain.

branches.if: Un resultado positivo
branches.example: Thanks to the team, it’s finished.

branches.if: Un contexto formal o escrito
branches.use: owing to / as a result of
branches.example: Owing to bad weather, the flight was cancelled.

items.note: Sin “being” + participio, la frase dice que la cosa repara algo.
“Being” solo va en el continuo; en el perfecto es “been”.

items.a: The flight was delayed due to fog.
items.b: The flight was delayed due to it was foggy.
items.note: “Due to” va con sustantivo, no con una cláusula.

items.example: I called to confirm.
We left early so as to avoid traffic.
The bay was sealed in order to run tests.
The policy was introduced with the aim of reducing costs.

branches.if: Propósito (¿para qué lo hice?)
branches.example: I went out to buy bread.

branches.if: Propósito negativo
branches.use: so as not to / in order not to
branches.example: I whispered so as not to wake the baby.

branches.if: Función de un objeto
branches.example: This knife is for cutting bread.

branches.if: Propósito con otro sujeto
branches.example: I left the key for you to open the door.

items.note: El “para + infinitivo” del español se dice solo con “to”.

items.a: I left early so as not to miss it.
items.b: I left early to not miss it.
items.note: La forma correcta del propósito negativo es “so as not to / in order not to”.

items.a: There’s too much noise for me to work.
items.b: There’s too much noise to me work.
items.note: Con otro sujeto: for + persona + to.

branches.if: Un verbo en forma base
branches.example: I’d rather walk.

branches.if: Un verbo con to
branches.example: I’d prefer to walk.

branches.if: Un sustantivo
branches.example: I’d prefer tea to coffee.

branches.if: Otra persona y su comportamiento
branches.example: I’d rather you didn’t smoke here.

steps.label: Con rather
steps.change: rather + verbo base … than + verbo base.

steps.label: Negativa
steps.sentence: I’d **rather not** drive. / I’d **prefer not to** drive.
steps.change: La negación va con rather / prefer.

items.note: “Would rather” nunca lleva “to”.
Con prefer, la comparación usa “to”.
Con otra persona, el verbo va en pasado aunque hable del futuro.

steps.label: Método negativo
steps.sentence: We saved time **by not repeating** the test.

branches.if: La acción que produce el resultado
branches.example: I learned English by watching series.

branches.if: La herramienta o el material
branches.example: Open it with a screwdriver.

branches.if: Una acción que no hiciste
branches.example: She left without saying goodbye.

branches.if: El medio de transporte
branches.example: We went by bus.

items.note: “By” es preposición: siempre va seguida de -ing.

items.a: Cut it by pressing the button.
items.note: “By” nombra una acción; “with” nombra una herramienta.
La primera nombra el método; la segunda, el propósito.

B1-9-0.title: ¿Lo hiciste tú o lo mandaste a hacer?

steps.label: Lo mandé a hacer
steps.change: have + objeto + participio: otra persona lo hizo.

steps.label: Algo que te pasó
steps.change: También sirve para cosas malas que te pasan.

branches.if: Tú hiciste el trabajo
branches.example: I painted the flat.

branches.if: Pediste o pagaste para que lo hicieran
branches.example: I had the flat painted.

branches.if: Quieres nombrar a quien lo hizo
branches.example: I had a painter do the flat.

branches.if: Convenciste a alguien
branches.example: I got my brother to paint the flat.

items.note: La primera: te lo cortaste tú mismo. La segunda: fuiste a la peluquería.
La primera dice que tú lo organizaste; la pasiva no lo menciona.

items.b: I had the car to repair.
items.note: La segunda significa “tenía que arreglar el carro”, no lo mismo.

items.example: It might be worth asking them.
We could ask them first.
How about asking them?
Why don’t we ask them?
We should ask them.
Let’s ask them.

branches.if: How about / What about
branches.example: How about meeting on Friday?

branches.if: Why don’t we / Let’s / We could
branches.example: Why don’t we meet on Friday?

branches.if: It might be better / The best thing is
branches.example: It might be better to meet on Friday.

branches.if: I suggest / I recommend
branches.example: I suggest meeting on Friday.

items.note: “How about” va con -ing, nunca con “to”.

items.b: Why don’t we to start now?
items.note: “Why don’t we” va con verbo base.
“Suggest” no lleva objeto + infinitivo.

B1-10-0.title: ¿Qué futuro necesito?
B1-10-0.question: ¿Qué forma tiene la acción en el futuro?

branches.if: Es una predicción o una decisión
branches.example: I think prices will rise.

branches.if: Estará en progreso en un momento futuro
branches.example: At ten tomorrow I’ll be flying.

branches.if: Estará terminada antes de una fecha
branches.example: By June I’ll have finished.

branches.if: Quieres decir cuánto tiempo llevará hasta entonces
branches.example: By May I’ll have been working here a year.

steps.label: En progreso
steps.sentence: This time tomorrow I **’ll be studying**.

steps.label: Terminado
steps.sentence: By Friday I **’ll have finished** the course.
steps.change: will have + participio: antes de la fecha.

items.a: At ten tomorrow I’ll be working.
items.b: By ten tomorrow I’ll have finished.
items.note: “At” + momento pide continuo; “by” + fecha límite pide perfecto.

items.a: By the time you arrive, we’ll have started.
items.b: By the time you will arrive, we’ll have started.
items.note: Después de “by the time” va presente, no “will”.

items.a: Will you be using the car tonight?
items.b: Will you use the car tonight?
items.note: La primera pregunta por planes con cortesía; la segunda puede sonar a petición.

branches.if: Cuánto duró o lleva (una duración)
branches.example: I’ve lived here for six years.

branches.if: Cuándo empezó (punto de inicio)
branches.example: I’ve lived here since 2020.

branches.if: Cuánto tiempo atrás pasó
branches.example: I moved here six years ago.

branches.if: Un período cerrado con inicio y fin
branches.example: I lived there from 2015 to 2019.

items.note: Con “since” se usa present perfect, no presente simple.

items.b: I have left two years ago.
items.note: “Ago” va solo con pasado simple.
“During” va con sustantivo; con una cláusula usa “while”.

B1-11-0.title: Nunca “will” en la cláusula de tiempo

steps.label: Error
steps.sentence: When I **will finish**, I’ll call you.

steps.label: Correcto
steps.change: Presente simple en la cláusula de tiempo.

steps.label: Énfasis en terminar
steps.sentence: Once I **’ve finished**, I’ll call you.
steps.change: Present perfect para resaltar que está terminado.

steps.label: Orden invertido
steps.sentence: I’ll call you **as soon as** I finish.
steps.change: Sin coma cuando la cláusula de tiempo va segunda.

B1-11-0.title: ¿Cuánto tiempo pasa entre las dos acciones?

items.example: The moment she arrived, the meeting started.
I’ll call you as soon as I land.
Once you’ve signed, we’ll send the copy.
When the shift ends, file the report.
After we eat, we’ll go for a walk.

branches.if: La acción continúa hasta ese momento y para
branches.example: We’ll wait until the permit arrives.

branches.if: Algo no pasa antes de ese momento
branches.example: We won’t start until the permit arrives.

branches.if: Algo ya estará hecho cuando llegue ese momento
branches.use: by the time + perfecto en la principal
branches.example: By the time you arrive, we’ll have finished.

steps.label: Arrepentimiento
steps.change: should have + participio: lo que debiste hacer.

steps.label: Resultado irreal
steps.sentence: If I had checked the log, I **would have seen** the error.

items.example: If we’d left earlier, we might have caught it.
If we’d left earlier, we could have caught it.
If we’d left earlier, we would have caught it.

items.note: La primera es un consejo para ahora; la segunda critica el pasado.

items.a: If I had known, I would have told you.
items.b: If I would have known, I would have told you.
items.note: En la cláusula con “if” va had + participio, no “would”.
“Should of” es un error de escritura de “should’ve”.

B1-12-0.title: ¿Cómo expreso el propósito?
B1-12-0.question: ¿Quién va a hacer la acción del propósito?

branches.if: El mismo sujeto de la frase
branches.example: I called to confirm the booking.

branches.if: Otra persona
branches.example: We stopped for the crew to rest.

branches.if: Otra persona y necesito un modal (can, could)
branches.example: I spoke slowly so that everyone could understand.

branches.if: La función de un objeto
branches.example: This key is for the side door.

steps.label: to
steps.sentence: We labelled the boxes **to avoid** confusion.

steps.label: in order to
steps.sentence: We labelled the boxes **in order to avoid** confusion.

steps.label: so that
steps.sentence: We labelled the boxes **so that nobody could** confuse them.
steps.change: Necesita sujeto y, a menudo, un modal.

items.note: “For” + verbo nunca expresa propósito.

items.a: We moved it so that she could sit.
items.b: We moved it for she could sit.
items.note: Con una cláusula se usa “so that”, no “for”.
Las dos son correctas para la función de un objeto.

branches.if: Una cláusula con información nueva
branches.example: We stopped because the pump failed.

branches.if: Una causa que ya se conoce, al inicio
branches.example: Since nobody replied, I decided myself.

branches.if: Un sustantivo o gerundio
branches.use: because of / due to / owing to
branches.example: The flight was delayed due to fog.

branches.if: Una explicación más elaborada
branches.example: The reason why we left is that it was late.

items.example: I left because I was tired.
We stayed in because of the rain.
As it was late, we took a taxi.
The delay was due to a strike.
Owing to bad weather, the event was postponed.

steps.label: Conjunción
steps.sentence: The flight was delayed **because the weather was bad**.

steps.label: Preposición
steps.sentence: The flight was delayed **because of the bad weather**.

steps.label: Marco nominal
steps.sentence: **The reason why** the flight was delayed **is that** the weather was bad.

items.example: She can’t have seen it — she was asleep.
He couldn’t have known.
They might not have received the email.
It might have been the cable.
She may have left early.
The seal must have failed.

steps.label: Imposible
steps.sentence: It **can’t have been** the cat — we don’t have one.

items.note: El negativo de deducción es “can’t have”; “mustn’t” es prohibición.

items.a: It might have been the cable.
items.note: La primera es una suposición; la segunda es un hecho.
El continuo indica que la acción estaba en progreso en ese momento.

branches.if: Fue un error, había que hacer otra cosa
branches.example: They should have tested it first.

branches.if: Había otra opción posible
branches.example: We could have waited a day.

branches.if: Lo que tú habrías hecho
branches.example: I would have called the client.

branches.if: No era posible hacer otra cosa
branches.example: They couldn’t have known.

items.example: You could have told me.
I would have waited.
They ought to have reported it.
They should have checked.

items.note: La primera deduce qué pasó; la segunda critica una decisión.
“Should” aconseja ahora; “should have” critica el pasado.
La primera es una oportunidad perdida; la segunda, una posibilidad futura.

steps.label: Pasiva
steps.change: is / are + participio; el agente no importa.

steps.label: Pasiva con modal
steps.sentence: The parts **must be cleaned** before use.

steps.label: Paso terminado
steps.sentence: Once the parts **have been cleaned**, they are inspected.

items.es: Una vez que se ha hecho…,

items.note: La primera es un paso rutinario; la segunda pasa ahora mismo.
“Must” es obligatorio; “should” es recomendación.
Sin “are” + participio, la frase no tiene sentido pasivo.

items.a: My brother who lives in Cali is a doctor.
items.b: My brother, who lives in Cali, is a doctor.
items.note: Sin comas: tengo varios hermanos y hablo del que vive en Cali. Con comas: tengo un solo hermano.

items.a: The students who passed got a prize.
items.b: The students, who passed, got a prize.
items.note: Sin comas: solo algunos aprobaron. Con comas: todos aprobaron.

items.a: The report that arrived late was rejected.
items.b: The report, which arrived late, was rejected.
items.note: Sin comas identifica cuál informe; con comas solo agrega un dato.

B1-14-1.title: ¿Con comas o sin comas?
B1-14-1.question: ¿Qué hace la cláusula en la frase?

branches.if: Dice cuál persona o cosa (sin ella no se entiende)
branches.example: The engineer who signed it has left.

branches.if: Agrega información extra sobre algo ya identificado
branches.example: Ana, who signed it, has left.

branches.if: Comenta toda la frase anterior
branches.example: The test failed twice, which delayed the launch.

steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: Medellín is in Antioquia. It has a metro.

steps.label: No definitoria
steps.sentence: Medellín, **which** has a metro, is in Antioquia.

steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: The bus goes to the airport. It leaves at six.

steps.label: Definitoria
steps.sentence: The bus **that** goes to the airport leaves at six.

items.example: The layout could be simplified.
The manual should be updated.
It ought to be changed monthly.
All entries have to be signed.
It must be approved by the director.
This has got to be fixed today!

steps.label: Con responsable
steps.sentence: The manual must be updated **by the safety officer**.

items.note: “Should” recomienda; “must” obliga.

items.a: This has got to be fixed!
items.note: “Has got to” es enfático e informal; en un informe escrito usa “must”.

items.b: Passwords don’t have to be shared.
items.note: “Mustn’t” prohíbe; “don’t have to” dice que no es necesario.

steps.label: Tag negativo
steps.change: Repite el auxiliar y cambia a negativo.

steps.label: Tag con do
steps.change: Si no hay auxiliar, usa do / does / did.

branches.if: Confirmar algo que ya crees (pedir acuerdo)
branches.example: It’s a great view, isn’t it? ↘

branches.if: Preguntar porque de verdad no sabes
branches.example: You’ve paid the bill, haven’t you? ↗

items.note: Con “I am” el tag es “aren’t I?”.
Con “let’s” el tag es “shall we?”.
“Nobody” es negativo, así que el tag es positivo, con “they”.

branches.if: Está terminado (last year, in 2021, yesterday)
branches.example: I finished the course in May.

branches.if: Sigue abierto (this year, so far, today)
branches.example: I’ve completed four modules this year.

branches.if: No mencionas cuándo, solo importa el resultado
branches.example: I’ve worked in four countries.

branches.if: Primero la experiencia, luego los detalles
branches.example: I’ve led a team. I led one in 2022.

items.note: Con una fecha terminada no se usa present perfect.
Con “since” para algo que continúa, usa present perfect.

items.a: I worked there for two years.
items.b: I’ve worked there for two years.
items.note: La primera: ya no trabajas ahí. La segunda: todavía trabajas ahí.

items.example: I’d like to have travelled more by then.
I hope to have finished by May.
I plan to apply in March.
By June I’ll have finished the course.

steps.label: Meta
steps.sentence: I want to finish the certification.

steps.label: Futuro perfecto
steps.sentence: **By December I’ll have finished** the certification.
steps.change: will have + participio: estará hecho antes de la fecha.

steps.label: Deseo
steps.sentence: **I’d like to have finished** the certification by December.
steps.change: would like to have + participio: lo que te gustaría haber logrado.

steps.label: Duración
steps.sentence: By December **I’ll have been studying** for a year.
steps.change: will have been + -ing: cuánto tiempo llevarás.

B1-16-1.title: Mirar hacia adelante o hacia atrás

items.a: I’d like to finish the course.
items.b: I’d like to have finished the course by June.
items.note: La primera mira hacia adelante desde hoy; la segunda mira hacia atrás desde junio.

items.a: By the time I’m thirty, I’ll have finished.
items.b: By the time I’ll be thirty, I’ll have finished.
items.note: Después de “by the time” va presente, no “will”.

items.a: I’ll have known her for ten years.
items.b: I’ll have been knowing her for ten years.
items.note: “Know” es verbo de estado: no se usa en continuo.
